comments.content: The new test only asserts that `animimg` (created in `setUp()` and already covered by `test_animimg_successful_create`) is not NULL, so it does not actually verify the behavior introduced by splitting `lv_animimg_set_src` into a forward and a reverse variant. Since the whole point of the change is the start/end animation range, assert the stored source information and the reversed animation range, e.g. via `lv_animimg_get_anim()`. The same weakness applies to the forward test `test_animimg_set_src`, which should check `start_value == 0` / `end_value == num`.

comments.content: `lv_animimg_set_src_reverse()` duplicates the source/count assignment of `lv_animimg_set_src()` line by line; the only difference is the animation value range. Any future change to source handling (e.g. caching the first frame, validating `num`, resetting the image) would have to be replicated in both places and can easily drift. Reuse `lv_animimg_set_src()` and only override the value range.

comments.content: The new name overloads an existing concept in this widget's API: `lv_animimg_set_reverse_duration()` / `lv_animimg_set_reverse_delay()` already use "reverse" to mean *ping-pong playback* (play back after the forward pass). `lv_animimg_set_src_reverse()` on the other hand only inverts the *frame order*. A user reading the API can easily assume it enables playback reversal. Please make the distinction explicit in the doc (and note that `lv_animimg_set_src()` resets the direction back to forward, so calling it after this function silently discards the reversed order).
comments.suggestion_code:
* Set the image animation source and play the frames in reverse order
 * (from the last image to the first one).
 * Note: unlike `lv_animimg_set_reverse_duration`, this does not enable
 * playback (ping-pong) of the animation, it only flips the frame order.
 * Calling `lv_animimg_set_src` afterwards restores the forward order.
